newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin sacks Lebed as envoy in rebel Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin sacks Lebed as envoy in rebel Chechnya.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin sacked General Alexander Lebed on Saturday as his personal representative in breakaway Chechnya, appointing moderate Ivan Rybkin in his place, the Kremlin press service said.

Yeltsin sacked Lebed on Thursday as his security supremo. Chechen separatists, with whom Lebed brokered a peace deal on August 31, have warned that Lebed's dismissal could lead to a deterioration of the situation there.
Yeltsin sacked Lebed dramatically from the Security Council on Thursday, accusing him in a televised speech of lack of team spirit and naked presidential ambitions.

Rybkin, who turns 50 on Sunday, was speaker of the State Duma lower house of parliament from 1993 to 1995. A communist, he was elected as a member of the conservative agrarian party, but broke with it after becoming head of the parliament and turning into a Yeltsin ally.

A moderate, Rybkin steered the Duma firmly away from any clashes with the president. After the election in 1995, he failed to win a second term as speaker because the communists and their allies voted against him.
